DEP 4, written in 2015, set a feature release every eight months, the rhythm since 1.8, and, from 2.0, series of three, X.0, X.1 and X.2, the last its long-term release (`deps:final/0004-release-schedule.rst`).
The releases that were to be 7.0 and 7.1 are Django 2028 and Django 2029 (`deps:accepted/0020-annual-release-cycle.rst`, `docs/releases/6.2.txt`).

This commit is main on 26 September 2026, a pre-alpha of 6.2 (`django/utils/version.py:get_version`); 6.1.1 is the newest release, and 6.2 is expected in April 2027.

The figure sets the releases in their years, from the release notes (`docs/releases/`) and, for [0.90](https://www.djangoproject.com/weblog/2005/nov/16/firstrelease/), [0.96](https://www.djangoproject.com/weblog/2007/mar/23/096/) and [1.0](https://www.djangoproject.com/weblog/2008/sep/03/1/), the project's announcements: look for the long-term releases, the two changes of rhythm, and where this commit stands.

Since 6.1, reading a field or a related object a queryset did not load follows a **fetch mode**: a fetch for that instance, as before (`FETCH_ONE`); one for it and its peers, other instances of its model the same run of the queryset made (`FETCH_PEERS`); or a refusal (`FETCH_RAISE`) (`django/db/models/fetch_modes.py`; [What changed in querysets](changes/querysets.md)).

**Services are configured by alias**: `TASKS` (6.0) and `MAILERS` (6.1) name their backends as `CACHES`, `DATABASES` and `STORAGES` already did, and the email settings `MAILERS` replaces are deprecated (`django/tasks/__init__.py:TaskBackendHandler`, `django/core/mail/handler.py:MailersHandler`; [What changed in mail and tasks](changes/mail-and-tasks.md)).

**Services are configured by alias**: `TASKS` (6.0) and `MAILERS` (6.1) name their backends as `CACHES`, `DATABASES` and `STORAGES` already did, and the email settings `MAILERS` replaces are deprecated (`django/tasks/__init__.py:TaskBackendHandler`, `django/core/mail/handler.py:MailersHandler`; [What changed in mail and tasks](changes/mail-and-tasks.md)).

Release after release added coroutine twins, such as `aauthenticate` and `Signal.asend` (5.0); then 6.2 made most of Django's own middleware synchronous only (`async_capable = False`), so that under ASGI a chain of it runs in a thread as one call around its centre, which stays on the event loop, instead of crossing into a thread and back for each hook (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.load_middleware`; [Sync and async in one chain](handlers/async.md)).

**Safer defaults**: time zone support (5.0), 64-bit automatic keys (6.0), `"https"` as the scheme a form's URL field assumes (6.0), and more iterations of the PBKDF2 password hasher in every feature release (`django/contrib/auth/hashers.py:PBKDF2PasswordHasher`).
The release process allows a change outright where a path through deprecation is not possible or not worth its cost (`docs/internals/release-process.txt`).

The old behaviour ordinarily stays for at least two feature releases and warns, some of its warnings only when the use comes from outside Django's own code (`django/utils/deprecation.py:warn_about_external_use`).

`RemovedInDjango2028Warning` is a `DeprecationWarning`, which Python shows by default only when the line it names is in the script Python runs; `RemovedInDjango2029Warning` is a `PendingDeprecationWarning`, which Python never shows by default (`django/utils/deprecation.py`).

Some deprecations come with a **transitional setting**, which lets a project take the new behaviour early or keep the old one for a time: at this commit `URLIZE_ASSUME_HTTPS`, `USE_BLANK_CHOICE_DASH` and `SIGNED_COOKIE_LEGACY_SALT_FALLBACK` (`django/conf/global_settings.py`; [What still warns: the deprecations and the releases that end them](changes/deprecations.md#settings)).

A model that declares no primary key and has no parent, such as journal's Entry, is given one, of the class that `DEFAULT_AUTO_FIELD` names unless its application names another (`django/db/models/options.py:Options._get_default_pk_class`).
6.0 changed the setting's default from `AutoField` to `BigAutoField`, and since then nothing warns (`django/conf/global_settings.py`):

A project upgraded to 6.0 that never named the class finds each such model's key a `BigAutoField`, and makemigrations writes an `AlterField` for each (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector.generate_altered_fields`).
Django's own calls name their algorithm, so only calls from outside Django warn (`django/utils/crypto.py:salted_hmac`, `django/core/signing.py:Signer.signature`).

At this commit `MiddlewareMixin`, the base class of nearly all Django's own middleware, lives in `django.middleware`, and its old module's `__getattr__` hands the class to an old import with a warning (`django/utils/deprecation.py:__getattr__`).
5.2 deprecated `login` given no user, which then logged in the request's user, and 6.1 removed the fallback (`docs/releases/5.2.txt`, `django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:login`).
